newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Two die in Sri Lanka rebel attack on Hindu temple.
newsitem.headline: Two die in Sri Lanka rebel attack on Hindu temple.

text.p: Two Sri Lankan girls were killed and 12 people wounded when Tamil Tiger rebels attacked a Hindu temple in eastern Batticaloa district on Sunday, a military spokesman said on Monday.

The temple, about 220 km (135 miles) from Colombo, came under rocket and mortar fire from the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) as the army's area brigade commander and a Tamil parliamentarian addressed residents, he said.
Troops used mortars and armoured vehicles to repulse the attack by the rebels, who are fighting for an independent homeland for minority Tamils in the north and east, he said.
"Twelve civilians and two soldiers were wounded in the attack," he said. "Two girls succumbed to their wounds in hospital."
The brigade commander and the politician were not injured in the attack.
LTTE rebels killed a policeman and wounded another in Batticaloa town the same day when they attacked a police post, the spokesman said.
The Tigers on Monday accused the security forces of abducting and killing Tamil civilians during search operations and dumping their bodies into the sea, but the military spokesman denied the charge.
"Young men and women taken into custody regularly disappear and many are now being killed and taken out to sea in naval boats or dropped from helicopters," the LTTE said in a statement.
More than 15 bodies were washed ashore at Mullaitivu on the northeast coast, about 280 kilometres (175 miles) from the capital, during the past week, it said.
"We no longer have troops at Mullaitivu," the military spokesman said. "This is the usual LTTE propaganda."

The LTTE accusation came at a time of growing fears among Tamil residents and politicians of an increase in human rights abuses by security forces in the mainly Tamil north of this Indian Ocean island.

Eleven servicemen accused of raping and killing a teenaged Tamil girl in northern Jaffna and killing her mother, brother and a neighbour who came looking for her, were due to appear in a Colombo court later on Monday.
The bodies of the victims were dumped in a salt pit.
The government has ordered an inquiry into the incident and assured the public it will not tolerate human rights abuses.
The government says more than 50,000 people have died in the war, now in its 14th year.
